title: How much line does an isometric box use?
description: A box one unit long, two units deep and three units tall is drawn on the grid. The board counts three visible edges in each direction, finds the units of line in each direction, and adds them. Keeko's doubt is that each length is drawn only once.
teaching_notes: One idea: a box seen from a corner has three visible edges in each direction, so each length is drawn three times. Watch for students who add the length, depth and height only once.

source: Draw a cuboid 1 unit long, 2 units deep and 3 units tall on
video_script.why: The child finds the units of line used by the visible edges of a box by taking each direction in turn.
video_script.substitution: Units of line = 3 x length + 3 x depth + 3 x height.
video_script.anchor: a box one unit long, two units deep and three units tall, drawn on the grid with its three hidden edges dotted at the back
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks only six units are used, because one plus two plus three is six. Each length is drawn on three edges, so three times six is eighteen.
video_script.payoff_line: The box uses eighteen units of line
maths_rules: a box seen from a corner shows 9 edges: 3 along the length, 3 along the depth, 3 along the height
slip: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 counts each length once; 3 x 6 = 18
video_script.design: The box drawn on the grid on the stage. The edges of each direction are traced in turn and a running total grows beside the box.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a box on the grid, 1 unit long, 2 units deep and 3 units tall

marks.box: the box appears on the grid with its three lengths marked
marks.ask: the visible edges of the box glow

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about drawing a box on the grid.
<bookmark mark='box'/>The box is one unit long, two units deep and three units tall.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many units of line do its visible edges use?

beats.on_screen: the box on the grid stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the box seen from a corner with nine edges; the three directions tinted; three hidden edges dotted at the back

marks.seen: the box is seen from a corner and nine edges are traced
marks.same: the three edges of one direction are tinted together
marks.dims: the length, the depth and the height are marked with three different numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='seen'/>Seen from a corner, a box shows nine edges, three in each direction.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The three edges in one direction all have the same length.
<bookmark mark='dims'/>The length, the depth and the height are three different numbers here.

beats.on_screen: Given: a box 1 unit long, 2 units deep and 3 units tall, drawn on the grid

marks.given: the three lengths of the box are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a box is one unit long, two units deep and three units tall.

beats.on_screen: To find: the units of line used by the visible edges

marks.find: the words units of line are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the units of line used by its visible edges.

beats.on_screen: Length: 3 visible edges, each 1 unit: 3 x 1 = 3

marks.len: the three edges along the length are traced and 3 x 1 = 3 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='len'/>Step one, take the length. Three visible edges run along the length, each one unit, so three times one is three.

beats.on_screen: Depth: 3 visible edges, each 2 units: 3 x 2 = 6

marks.dep: the three edges along the depth are traced and 3 x 2 = 6 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='dep'/>Step two, take the depth. Three visible edges run along the depth, each two units, so three times two is six.

beats.on_screen: Height: 3 visible edges, each 3 units: 3 x 3 = 9

marks.hei: the three edges along the height are traced and 3 x 3 = 9 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='hei'/>Step three, take the height. Three visible edges run along the height, each three units, so three times three is nine.

marks.sum: the three results are added and 3 + 6 + 9 = 18 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step four, add the three directions. Three plus six plus nine makes eighteen units.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The box uses eighteen units of line.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the box
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 1 + 2 + 3 = 6; the three edges of each direction are tinted; the bubble is struck through

marks.three: the three edges of each direction are tinted, so each length appears three times
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and 3 x 6 = 18 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks only six units are used, because one plus two plus three is six.
<bookmark mark='three'/>But each length is drawn on three edges, not on one.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Each length counts three times, and three times six is eighteen.
